reason: The proof is a complete direct verification from the stated definition of the Gaussian q-binomial coefficient. Under 0 <= r <= n, both r and n-r are nonnegative, so both defining expressions are legitimate. Substituting s = n-r into the formula gives [n choose n-r]_q = (q;q)_n / ((q;q)_{n-r}(q;q)_r), and commutativity of multiplication identifies this denominator with ((q;q)_r (q;q)_{n-r}), which is exactly the denominator for [n choose r]_q. Hence the two expressions are identical as polynomials in q. There is no reliance on the root theorem or other forbidden dependencies.
